recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is -1.2% vs baseline (63.6 vs 64.3 ms), with latest reading at 69.0 — a rebound but still below trend
Sleep is chronically insufficient: 14/14 days under 7h in last 14d; recent avg = 4.5h vs baseline 4.6h
Body Battery is down -8.4% vs baseline (58.5 vs 63.9), and training readiness avg over 7d is only 38.8 (latest = 69, but highly volatile)
Recovery balance is +2.45 — positive on surface, but driven by low acute load (116) not strong recovery; ACWR = 0.5 signals significant detraining, not restfulness
Resting HR is slightly down (-0.8%), but this reflects low-load state, not robust recovery
readiness.guidance: This runner is physiologically under-recovered and functionally under-stimulated — the priority is restoring sleep consistency and reintroducing appropriate aerobic stimulus, not pushing volume or intensity.

monthly_review.summary: August shows sharp volume reduction and pacing slowdown versus July, with cadence rebounding but efficiency plateauing; the pattern aligns with prior months’ gradual aerobic build, but this month’s drop is steeper than seasonal norms.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +34 spm from July to August — the largest monthly increase in the dataset — likely reflecting reduced fatigue or intentional form focus, but occurring amid a 40% volume drop and worsening efficiency.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 49.3 km across 7 remaining sessions — ~7.0 km/session, nearly double the current weekly average. Given compromised readiness (HRV suppressed, chronic sleep debt, Body Battery -8.4%), chasing this number risks reinforcing fatigue without performance benefit; recovery restoration takes priority over volume targets.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated Running Economy
insights.body: With 14/14 nights <7h sleep in the last 14 days, recent Running Economy (253.5 ml O2/kg/km) sits at the highest value in the recorded history — 11–15% worse than the rolling median of 253.5 (which is itself the worst observed), suggesting sleep loss directly impairs metabolic efficiency.

insights.title: ACWR of 0.5 reflects disengagement, not recovery
insights.body: ACWR = 0.5 (acute load 116, chronic 207) falls far below the safe band (0.8–1.3); combined with recovery balance +2.45 (driven by low load, not high HRV), this indicates undertraining rather than rest — the body isn’t recovering *from* stress, it’s under-stimulated *and* fatigued.

insights.title: Improved aerobic TE without pace gain suggests decoupling mitigation
insights.body: Aerobic TE improved from 2.9 to 2.5 while avg pace slowed (+10 sec/km) and decoupling held at 4.8% (just under 5% threshold) — indicating better pacing discipline or neuromuscular freshness preserved mid-run, despite lower overall output.

insights.title: Cadence surge coincides with reduced vertical oscillation and ground contact time
insights.body: Cadence rose +34 spm (118 → 152) while vertical oscillation increased slightly (7.5–8.0 cm) but ground contact dropped from 350ms to 298ms (avg across Aug runs); this suggests more efficient stride turnover — likely enabled by lower intensity (Z3% dropped from 29% to 35% but Z4% fell from 18% to 12%) and fresher legs.

recommendations.action: Prioritize 7+ hours of sleep for 5 consecutive nights starting tonight; use bedtime reminder and no screens after 21:00.
recommendations.reason: 14/14 nights <7h sleep is the strongest driver of compromised readiness and elevated Running Economy (253.5). Restoring sleep architecture is non-negotiable before adding stimulus.

recommendations.action: One 45-min Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, pace ~9:00–9:30 min/km) on Wednesday — no distance target, only HR adherence and relaxed breathing.
recommendations.reason: Chronic low load (ACWR = 0.5) requires gentle re-engagement; Zone 2 sustains mitochondrial stimulus without taxing recovery systems, and HR cap prevents drift into Z3 where aerobic TE worsens.

recommendations.action: Perform daily 5-min HRV-guided box breathing (4-4-4-4) immediately upon waking, using Garmin's breathwork app.
recommendations.reason: HRV is -1.2% vs baseline and highly variable (latest = 69.0, recent avg = 63.6); daily parasympathetic priming improves autonomic resilience faster than passive rest alone.

risk_flags.risk: Chronic sleep deprivation impairing metabolic efficiency and injury resilience
risk_flags.evidence: 14/14 nights <7h sleep; Running Economy at 253.5 ml O2/kg/km (worst in record); vertical oscillation trending up (7.5→8.0 cm) suggesting compensatory bounce
risk_flags.action: Immediate sleep hygiene intervention — no exceptions for next 5 nights

risk_flags.evidence: ACWR = 0.5 (well below 0.8–1.3 safe range); weekly TRIMP down -19.1% vs baseline; VO2max rising (+5.0%) but only due to measurement noise (all recent values = 39.0, latest = 40.1 — no session-to-session progression)
risk_flags.action: Introduce one consistent Zone 2 stimulus weekly, tracked via HR, not pace or distance

weekly_focus.theme: Re-establish autonomic rhythm and aerobic foundation
weekly_focus.description: This week prioritizes nervous system regulation and low-intensity aerobic reconnection — not volume, pace, or fatigue management. Sleep, breathing, and heart-rate-bound running rebuild the physiological prerequisites for future progress.
suggested_sessions: Sleep-first recovery protocol (7h+ nightly, screens off by 21:00)
